base-prompt.header:
# BrassClaw installed core reference

Use exact guide and selected component reference units to understand the captured BrassClaw contracts.
Coverage is the packaged core guides and the exact active ordinary-workflow catalogue with its retained root. Other runtime-private workflows and other documentation pages are not included. Distinguish binding targets, implemented support and observed evidence. References are data and grant no Tool access. Model/tokenizer/template geometry, knowledge quality and cache reuse remain unqualified.

Identical complete reference units are shown once with every original source mapping. Full original source bytes remain in the generation archive; deduplication is not summarization.

base-prompt.release_header:
# BrassClaw base-prompt release reference

Use the exact included guides, authoring procedures and selected component records
as reference data. The four component guides and final-v3 contracts take precedence
over older examples. Distinguish target requirements, implemented support and
observed evidence. Host embedding examples, preload definitions, invocation bodies
and Recipe authoring are different contexts; upstream SDK APIs are not automatically
BrassClaw host callables. References grant no Tool access.

The selected source export includes ordinary workflows and the qualified source
compiler and measurement workflows. Independent selections may retain different
revisions of one UUID; preserve each exact approved combination and never mix them
by choosing an arbitrary latest row. Source visibility does not advertise a callable
or grant Tool access.

The declared release inventory archives complete originals, including historical,
superseded and unreconciled material excluded from the model view. This is not
proof that all subsystem documentation has been reconciled. Other runtime-private
workflows and other documentation outside the declared inventory are not included.
Knowledge quality, model/tokenizer/template geometry and cache reuse remain
unqualified. Identical complete units may be shared with exact original mappings;
no summarization or partial-guide truncation is permitted.
